summary: Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Leipzig under Georg von der Gabelentz and Ernst Windisch, and in Berlin and under Friedrich Max Müller and Tetsujiro Inoue. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and Hamburg (1914–1935).

Karl Friedrich Geldner was an Indologist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Leipzig and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch. He taught at Tübingen (1876–1887), Halle (1887–1890), Berlin (1890), and Marburg (1907–1921).
Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College, Harvard College (~1954–1958), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl H. Potter worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California (~1946–1950) and at Harvard University (1955) under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1971) and the University of Washington (~1971–1997).

Karl Hoffmann specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich (1934–1951) under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst, and later held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning his doctorate at the University of Vienna (1936–1941). He held positions at Weltmuseum Wien (~1948–1958), the University of Vienna (1958), Mainz (1961), and Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at Mainz (1787–1796) and Würzburg (1792–1796). He held posts at Lyceum Hosianum (1803), Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1811), and the University of Bonn (1818).

Karl Lachmann was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Leipzig University (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815), and later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1825–1851).

Karl Otfried Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. After teaching at Magdalenaeum Wrocław (1818–1819), he held a professorship at the University of Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), the London School of Economics (1946), King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Halle, Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel, and Heidelberg. He held academic posts at the University of Halle (~1828–1833) and the University of Königsberg (from 1833).

Karl Verner worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole and the University of Copenhagen under August Leskien, and held posts as librarian at the University of Halle (~1876–1883) and lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen (1882).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Augsburg and the University of Munich, and held posts at Munich (1978–1988), the Munich School of Politics (1989–1991), and the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn (~1978–1985) and his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg (~1993–1999). He was a Privatdozent at Hamburg (1999) and a researcher at Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1991–2018).
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as the main student under Anagarika Govinda from ~1968 to 1985, succeeding him between 1982 and 1999.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under Tenzin Gyatso and earned a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi. She held posts at the University of San Diego (2000–2022) and the University of Hawaiʻi (2023).

Karma Phuntsho is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Oxford under Michael Aris, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Richard Gombrich, and at Sera and Ngagyur Nyingma. He held posts at CNRS (~2003–2005) and the University of Cambridge (~2003–2012).

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She completed Shastri and Acharya degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned a PhD at the University of Tasmania under Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.
Karma Thinley Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He served as abbot at Young Lamas Home School (~1963–1968) and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling (~1973).
